title: Identity component of an unramified field groupoid
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme and $(U,R,s,t,e,i,c)$ a groupoid in algebraic spaces over $S$, with $U=\operatorname{Spec}K$ for a field $K$ [def-weil-field]. Assume $s,t:R\to U$ are locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] and $j=(s,t):R\to U\times_SU$ is unramified [def-weil-unramified-morphism]. Then $R$ is a separated scheme, a disjoint union of spectra of local Artinian rings finite-dimensional over $K$ via either projection. The map $j$ is separated and locally quasi-finite. Here separated means its diagonal is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion], and locally quasi-finite means locally of finite type with discrete finite-type field fibres. The open and closed component $P=\operatorname{Spec}B$ containing the point $e(U)$ has $B$ local Artinian, with residue field identified with $K$ by both projections. The groupoid operations restrict to $P$, the maps $s|_P,t|_P:P\to U$ are finite locally free [def-pc-finite-locally-free], and $j|_P:P\to U\times_SU$ is a monomorphism. Thus on every test scheme $P$ defines an equivalence relation on $U$. Artinian means descending chains of ideals stabilize, local means one maximal ideal, and monomorphism means injectivity on every test-scheme Hom set. A groupoid in algebraic spaces means objects $U$ and arrows $R$ with source $s$, target $t$, unit $e$, inverse and composition giving groupoids on all test-scheme points, naturally under pullback; for schemes these are [def-a1-groupoid-scheme]. Algebraic spaces and fibre products use [def-trf-algebraic-space], [def-pc-fibre-product]; space morphism properties are tested on etale scheme charts.

proof.text: Put $Y=U\times_SU$ and $G=U\times_{\Delta_{U/S},Y,j}R$. This is an algebraic space by [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Its map to $U$ is a base change of $j$, hence unramified by [lem-sfb-space-unramified-permanence]. Choose an etale surjective scheme chart $V\to G$ using [def-trf-algebraic-space]. The chart is unramified and its composite $V\to G\to U$ is unramified, again by the etale and composition clauses of [lem-sfb-space-unramified-permanence]. Thus [lem-trf-unramified-field-fibre-decomposition] makes $V$ a disjoint union of spectra of finite separable extensions of $K$. Every such chart has dimension zero. The chartwise dimension convention in [lem-sfb-field-groupoid-stabilizer-dimension] gives $\dim G=0$ (the unit gives a point of $G$), and its dimension equality gives $\dim R=0$. Both locally finite type projections required by that equality are hypotheses of this item.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-zero-dimensional-field-space-components] to $(R,s)$ and to $(R,t)$. Thus $R$ is a separated scheme with one-point open and closed components, each the spectrum of a local Artinian algebra finite-dimensional over $K$ for either structure. These are the same components for both applications because they are the individual underlying points of $R$. Let $P=\operatorname{Spec}B$ be the component containing $e(U)$ and write $\epsilon=e^\sharp:B\to K$. This is defined because the unit factors through that open component. The equations $se=te=1$ give $\epsilon s^\sharp=\epsilon t^\sharp=1_K$. Therefore $\epsilon$ is surjective, its kernel is the unique maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$ of $B$, and $B/\mathfrak m\simeq K$ via $\epsilon$, with both structural field maps inducing the identity of $K$.

source.place: Tag 06N0 (lemma-DM-residual-gerbe), Artinian decomposition and the identity component; Tags 06LZ and 06LH.

proof.text: For each of the two $K$-structures on $B$, choose a finite vector-space basis beginning with $1$. It exhibits $B$ as a finite free $K$-module; tensoring a module with $B$ is a finite direct sum, so preserves injections and exact sequences. It also gives an explicit finite algebra presentation: introduce a variable for each basis vector other than $1$, and impose the finitely many multiplication-table relations $x_i x_j=\sum_k c_{ijk}x_k$, writing $x_1=1$. Every polynomial reduces to a linear combination of the basis vectors, and their linear independence proves that the resulting presentation maps isomorphically onto $B$. Thus both maps $P\to U$ are finite, flat and of finite presentation, hence finite locally free by [def-pc-finite-locally-free].

source.place: Tag 06N0 (lemma-DM-residual-gerbe), finite flat maps from the identity component; explicit finite-basis argument for finite local freeness.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-artinian-local-noetherian-nilpotent] choose $N\ge1$ with $\mathfrak m^N=0$. For any choices of the two structural $K$-maps on the two factors of $B\otimes_KB$, the ideal $I=\mathfrak m\otimes_K B+B\otimes_K\mathfrak m$ satisfies $I^{2N}=0$, and the quotient is $K\otimes_KK=K$, because both residue structural maps are the identity. Consequently every prime contains $I$ and the tensor spectrum has exactly one point, with residue field $K$. In particular the space of composable arrows $P\times_{s,U,t}P$ has one point, represented by the pair of units. Composition sends this point to $e(U)$ by the unit axiom, and hence factors through the open $P\subset R$. Inversion also preserves that point, so factors through $P$. The unit already factors through $P$. Their identities hold after restriction because equality of maps into an open subscheme is tested after its inclusion. Thus all groupoid operations restrict to $P$, using the axioms of [def-a1-groupoid-scheme].

source.place: Tag 06N0 (lemma-DM-residual-gerbe), the assertion that P defines a subgroupoid, with its omitted tensor and restriction argument written out; nilpotence input Tag 00J8.

proof.text: Choose an affine open $W=\operatorname{Spec}A\subset Y$ containing the point $j(P)$. The map $P\to Y$ factors through $W$, since $P$ has one point. The projection $Y\to U$ makes $A$ a $K$-algebra and $A\to B$ compatible with the source $K$-structure. Therefore $D=P\times_Y P=P\times_W P=\operatorname{Spec}(B\otimes_A B)$ is a closed subscheme of $\operatorname{Spec}(B\otimes_{K,s,s}B)$: the tensor map is surjective, since every pure tensor is in its image. By the preceding nilpotent-ideal calculation this latter spectrum has one point; $D$ is nonempty because it has the diagonal $P\to D$. Hence $D$ has exactly one point. Restricting the now scheme morphism $j$ to $P\to W$ is unramified by [lem-weil-pbc-unramified-base-change-open]. Its diagonal $P\to D$ is an open immersion by [def-weil-unramified-morphism]. It is surjective on the one-point space, so is an isomorphism by [def-weil-open-immersion]. This proves monicity directly: two test-scheme maps $a,b:T\to P$ with $ja=jb$ form a map $T\to D$; its factorization through the isomorphic diagonal forces $a=b$.

source.place: Tag 06N0 (lemma-DM-residual-gerbe), monicity of P to U times U; equivalent diagonal proof expanding the Tag 05VH argument; scheme restriction Tag 02G6.

proof.text: The morphism $j$ is locally quasi-finite by [lem-weil-pbc-unramified-quasi-finite-at-points], since both $R$ and $Y$ are now schemes and $j$ is unramified by hypothesis. Its diagonal is the pullback of the absolute diagonal $R\to R\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z}R$ along the forgetful map $R\times_YR\to R\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z}R$: on every test scheme both pullbacks say that the two arrows to $R$ are equal. The absolute diagonal is closed because $R$ is separated by [lem-sfb-zero-dimensional-field-space-components]. Its pullback is closed directly from the affine quotient characterization in [def-weil-closed-immersion]: base change replaces $A/J$ by $A^\prime/JA^\prime$. Thus $j$ is separated. Finally on every $S$-scheme $T$, the restricted unit gives reflexivity, inversion gives symmetry, and restricted composition gives transitivity of the image of $P(T)$ in $U(T)\times U(T)$; the monicity just proved identifies $P(T)$ with that relation.
